proposed.text: How does the secondary mortgage market (operated by NHMFC) enable continuous housing loan availability?

options.text: It limits the number of loans primary lenders can issue, ensuring that only the most qualified applicants receive funding, thereby maintaining a stable financial environment
It guarantees that all housing loans will be paid without default, providing a safety net for lenders and encouraging them to issue more loans
It purchases loans from primary lenders (Pag-IBIG, banks), replenishing their capital so they can originate new loans
It replaces primary lenders entirely and becomes the sole source of housing finance, centralizing the loan process under one entity

proposed.rationale: NHMFC buys loans from primary lenders, converting those loans into investment instruments. This returns capital to the lender, enabling them to issue new loans rather than waiting for repayment. This recycling mechanism is essential for loan availability. [A]: Secondary market increases lending capacity, not limits it. [B]: NHMFC does not guarantee loan repayment; it is a purchaser of loans. [C]: NHMFC buys loans from primary lenders, converting those loans into investment instruments. This returns capital to the lender, enabling them to issue new loans rather than waiting for repayment. This recycling mechanism is essential for loan availability. [D]: NHMFC complements primary lenders; it does not replace them.
proposed.explanation: Secondary market increases lending capacity, not limits it. NHMFC does not guarantee loan repayment; it is a purchaser of loans. This recycling mechanism is essential for loan availability. NHMFC complements primary lenders; it does not replace them.
